summary: A massive wave of Russian drone and missile strikes hit Kyiv and multiple Ukrainian oblasts on September 21, 2026, targeting residential areas with Shahed drones and Geran-5 missiles. Ukrainian forces reported liberating two settlements in Donetsk as part of Operation Vivaldi, expanding liberated territory to 43.5 km². The Russian Ministry of Defense announced intensified strikes on Kyiv military objects in retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure.
key_points: Multiple Shahed drones and a Geran-5 missile struck Kyiv and the Kyiv region, hitting Boyarka, Borshchahivka, Darnytsia, Nyvky, and Vasylkiv, with at least one drone confirmed downed at 50 meters near Sofiivska Borshchahivka (Source: @mon1tor_ua/75308).
Ukrainian forces liberated Shandrigolove and Derylove in Donetsk as part of Operation Vivaldi, with a total liberated area of 43.5 km² (Source: @UkraineNow/84196).
The Russian MoD reported that UAV operators destroyed Ukrainian personnel at the Krasnooskolske reservoir (Source: @tass_agency/396501).
The Ukrainian Armed Forces attempted a massive attack using UAVs and Flamingo missiles to disrupt Russian elections on September 19–20 (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33386).
Approximately 11 regular UAVs were launched from the Black Sea toward Tatarbunary on Odessa Oblast in a mass attack (Source: @eRadarrua/114939).
Russian tactical aviation launched guided aerial bombs (KABs) on Zaporizhzhia Oblast and struck Mykolaiv with two KABs (Source: @kpszsu/79252, @mon1tor_ua/75343).
The Russian MoD stated it will intensify strikes on Ukrainian military objects in Kyiv in response to AFU attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure (Source: @UkraineNow/84203).
A Ukrainian soldier assessed that Russian forces may attempt to enter Zaporozhye with small infantry groups this winter (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33383).

sections.executive_summary: On September 21, 2026, Russia launched a large-scale combined drone and missile assault on Kyiv and multiple Ukrainian oblasts, deploying Shahed drones, Geran-5 missiles, and guided aerial bombs across at least ten regions. Ukrainian forces simultaneously advanced in Donetsk, liberating two settlements under Operation Vivaldi. The Russian Ministry of Defense threatened intensified strikes on Kyiv military infrastructure, citing Ukrainian attacks on Russian civilian targets as justification.
ukraine: Ukrainian forces liberated Shandrigolove and Derylove in Donetsk Oblast as part of Operation Vivaldi, with a total liberated area of 43.5 km², according to Deep State mapping data (Source: @UkraineNow/84196).

The Armed Forces of Ukraine attempted a massive attack using UAVs and Flamingo missiles to disrupt the expression of will of Russian citizens during the September 19–20 State Duma elections (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33386).
Railway services across Ukraine were delayed by up to 14 hours due to Russian attacks, according to Ukrainian Railways (Source: @UkraineNow/84197).
A massive fire broke out at EcoMarket warehouses near Kyiv, with the entire facility fully engulfed in flames (Source: @UkraineNow/84202).
A high-speed target struck the already burning Kapotne oil refinery, confirmed by moment-of-impact footage (Source: @UkraineNow/84198).
Ukrainian forces advanced near Shandrigolove following the liberation of Shandrigolove and Derylove, according to updated Deep State map data (Source: @DeepStateUA/23845).
A Shahed drone was confirmed shot down near Sofiivska Borshchahivka, descending from 1,400 meters to 100 meters before being destroyed at approximately 50 meters altitude (Source: @mon1tor_ua/75308).
russia: The Russian Ministry of Defense reported that UAV operators destroyed Ukrainian personnel at the Krasnooskolske reservoir, publishing associated video evidence (Source: @tass_agency/396501).

The Russian Ministry of Defense announced it will intensify strikes on Ukrainian military objects in Kyiv, citing Ukrainian attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure as the trigger (Source: @UkraineNow/84203).
The Russian MoD reported that the Armed Forces of Ukraine attempted a massive UAV and Flamingo missile attack during the September 19–20 elections (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33386).
Russian tactical aviation launched guided aerial bombs on Zaporizhzhia Oblast, according to Ukrainian monitoring data (Source: @kpszsu/79252).
A Ukrainian soldier, Dmitry Filatov, assessed that Russian forces may attempt to enter Zaporozhye with small infantry groups during winter (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33383).
The Central Election Commission reported United Russia at 57.7% after processing 64.98% of protocols in the State Duma elections (Source: @tass_agency/396492).
United Russia retained leadership in all single-mandate districts in Moscow after processing over 90% of protocols (Source: @tass_agency/396510).

air_war: Multiple Shahed drones struck Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast, including Boyarka (at least three separate incidents), Borshchahivka, Darnytsia district, Nyvky, and Vasylkiv (Source: @mon1tor_ua/75329, @mon1tor_ua/75340, @mon1tor_ua/75338, @mon1tor_ua/75327, @kpszsu/79249).

key_developments: Russia launched a mass drone and missile assault on Kyiv and at least ten Ukrainian oblasts on September 21, deploying Shahed drones, Geran-5 missiles, and KABs targeting residential areas and infrastructure, representing the largest single-day attack in recent weeks (Source: @mon1tor_ua, @kpszsu, @eRadarrua).

Ukrainian forces liberated Shandrigolove and Derylove in Donetsk Oblast under Operation Vivaldi, expanding liberated territory by 43.5 km² and advancing near Shandrigolove (Source: @UkraineNow/84196, @DeepStateUA/23845).

The Russian MoD announced intensified strikes on Kyiv military objects in retaliation for Ukrainian attacks on Russian civilian infrastructure, signaling further escalation of the capital's targeting (Source: @UkraineNow/84203).

The AFU attempted a massive UAV and Flamingo missile attack to disrupt Russian State Duma elections on September 19–20, marking a significant escalation targeting Russian domestic political processes (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33386).

A Shahed drone was confirmed shot down at only 50 meters altitude near Sofiivska Borshchahivka northwest of Kyiv, indicating successful Ukrainian air defense engagement at extremely low altitude (Source: @mon1tor_ua/75308).

Russian tactical aviation deployed guided aerial bombs on Zaporizhzhia Oblast while simultaneously launching UAVs from Black Sea waters toward Odessa, demonstrating multi-axis offensive operations (Source: @kpszsu/79252, @eRadarrua/114939).

A Ukrainian soldier assessed that Russian forces may attempt to enter Zaporozhye with small infantry groups during winter, indicating potential forthcoming ground operations in southern Ukraine (Source: @ukr_leaks_eng/33383).
sections.threat_assessment: The September 21 mass drone and missile assault on Kyiv and multiple oblasts demonstrates Russia's continued capacity for large-scale aerial operations despite Ukrainian air defense successes. The confirmed shootdown of a Shahed at 50 meters near Borshchahivka indicates effective terminal-phase interception but also highlights the persistent threat to civilian areas. The Russian MoD's explicit threat to intensify strikes on Kyiv military objects signals further escalation potential. The assessment that Russian forces may attempt to enter Zaporozhye with infantry groups this winter adds a ground-component threat to the already active air campaign.
sections.regional_response: Ukrainian air defense systems across multiple oblasts engaged incoming drones and missiles, with confirmed interceptions near Borshchahivka and in the Kyiv area. Ukrainian Railways reported delays of up to 14 hours nationwide due to attack disruptions. The Ukrainian military's simultaneous liberation of settlements in Donetsk under Operation Vivaldi indicates that Ukrainian offensive operations continue despite the heavy aerial bombardment. The AFU's attempted Flamingo missile and UAV attack on Russian election infrastructure represents a significant escalation in targeting Russian domestic political processes.
sections.intelligence_notes: The coordinated nature of the September 21 attacks, spanning at least ten oblasts with multiple drone types (Shaheds, reactive UAVs, regular UAVs) and guided bombs, suggests a centralized Russian operational command directing simultaneous strikes across multiple axes. The Russian MoD's claim of destroying Ukrainian personnel at Krasnooskolske reservoir via UAVs, combined with the reported Flamingo missile attack on election infrastructure, indicates a dual-track strategy of battlefield attrition and political disruption. The winter assessment regarding potential Russian infantry entry into Zaporozhye should be monitored as a possible indicator of forthcoming ground operations.
